1.word_for_word: aṣṭame — in the eighth chapter; nāma-karma — the naming rite; asya — of Him; bāla-krīḍā-kutūhale — in the marvels of childhood play; mṛd-bhakṣaṇa-abhiyoge — when He is accused of eating clay; ca — and; viśva-rūpam — the universal form; nirūpyate — is described; viśva-rūpa-ādi-bālasya — of the child whose wonders include the universal form; niśamya — having heard; āśaṅkinaḥ pituḥ — of the apprehensive father; nāma-kṛt-garga-vākyena — through the words of Garga, who performed the naming; nijam tattvam — His own true nature; asūsucat — He indicated.
1.translation: In the eighth chapter His naming rite, the marvels of His childhood play, and the universal form revealed when He is accused of eating clay are described. Having heard of the child's universal form and other wonders, His father became apprehensive; through the words of Garga, who performed the naming, He indicated His own true nature.

4.word_for_word: pūrṇaḥ cet — if he is already complete; kathaṃ dhanināṃ gṛham āgataḥ — why has he come to the house of householders possessing wealth?; tatra āha — to this he says; mahat-vicalanam — the movement of great souls; mahatām sva-āśramāt anyatra vicalanam — the going of great persons away from their own āśrama; na sva-artham — is not for their own sake; kintu gṛhiṇām maṅgalāya — but for the welfare of householders; nanu tarhi — but then; mahad-darśanārtham kim iti na āgacchanti — why do the householders not themselves go to see the great?; dīna-cetasām kṛpaṇānām — of the poor-minded, miserly householders; kṣaṇam api gṛham tyaktum aśaknuvatām — unable to leave home even for a moment.
4.translation: If he is already complete, why has he come to the house of wealthy householders? To this Nanda says, 'the movement of great souls.' Great persons leave their own āśramas and go elsewhere not for their own sake but for the welfare of householders. One may then ask why the householders do not themselves go to see the great. The answer is that these poor-minded, miserly people are unable to leave their homes even for a moment.

5.word_for_word: tvayā bālayoḥ nāma-karaṇa-ādi karaṇīyam — the naming and other rites of the two boys are to be performed by you; iti vaktum — in order to say this; tasya jñāna-atiśayam āha — he states the excellence of Garga's knowledge; yat atīndriya-jñānam — that knowledge which is beyond the senses; asādhanam — not obtainable by ordinary means; jyotiṣām ayanam — 'the course of the luminaries'; tat-pratipādakam jyotiḥ-śāstram — the Jyotiṣa scripture that teaches it; tat sākṣāt bhavatā praṇītam — that was directly composed by you; yena anyaḥ api pumān — by which even another person; parāvaram veda — knows the higher and the lower; param kāraṇam — the higher, the cause; pūrva-janma-kṛtam karma — action done in a previous birth; avaram kāryam — the lower, the effect; tasmin janmani bhāvi-phalam — the fruit to occur in this birth; yad upacitam anya-janmani śubhāśubham — the auspicious and inauspicious karma accumulated in another birth; tasya karmaṇaḥ paṅktim vyañjayati śāstram etat — this science reveals the sequence of that karma; tamasi dīpa iva — like a lamp in darkness.
5.translation: To say that the naming and other rites of the two boys should be performed by Garga, Nanda states the excellence of his knowledge. The suprasensory knowledge that cannot be reached by ordinary means is taught by the Jyotiṣa scripture called 'the course of the luminaries,' and that scripture was directly composed by you. Through it even another person knows the higher and lower: the higher is the causal karma performed in a previous birth, and the lower is its result that is to occur in the present birth. As it is said in the Jātaka: this science reveals the sequence of a person's auspicious and inauspicious karma accumulated in another birth, like a lamp revealing things in darkness.

6.word_for_word: vivakṣitam āha — he states what he intends to say; tvam hi — 'you indeed'; daivajñaḥ — a knower of destiny/astrology; mantravit ca — and a knower of mantra; tvam — you; ataḥ — therefore; nāma-karaṇa-ādi-saṃskārān — the rites beginning with naming; kartum arhasi — are qualified to perform; nanu etat guruṇā karaṇīyam — objection: this should be performed by a guru; iti cet — if so; tatra āha nṝṇām iti — to this he replies with 'of men.'
6.translation: He states what he intends with the words 'you indeed.' You are both a knower of Jyotiṣa and a knower of mantra; therefore you are qualified to perform the rites beginning with naming. If one objects that such rites ought to be performed by a guru, he answers with the words 'for men.'

7.word_for_word: atyutsāhinam nandam prati — addressing the exceedingly eager Nanda; guptam etat kāryam — this act must be kept secret; iti abhiprāyeṇa — with this intention; pratyācakṣāṇaḥ iva āha — he speaks as though declining; sutam iti — with the words concerning the son; kaṃsaḥ manyate — Kaṃsa 'thinks'; manyeta kalpayet — that is, he may suppose or imagine.
7.translation: Addressing the exceedingly eager Nanda, and intending that this act must be kept secret, Garga speaks as though declining it, beginning with the statement about the son. 'Kaṃsa thinks' has the sense 'Kaṃsa may suppose or imagine.'

8.word_for_word: nanu — objection; yadu-kumāra iti kathañcit jānātu — let Kaṃsa somehow learn only that the child is a Yadu boy; tatra vasudevasya sutaḥ — but how would he know that he is Vasudeva's son; tatra api devakyām jātaḥ — and moreover born of Devakī; iti kutaḥ jānīyāt — how could he know that?; tatra āha — to this Garga says; pāpa-matiḥ iti-ādi — beginning with 'Kaṃsa, whose mind is sinful.'
8.translation: One may object: let Kaṃsa somehow learn that the child is a Yadu boy; how could he know that the child is Vasudeva's son and, more specifically, that he was born of Devakī? To this Garga replies with the words beginning, 'Kaṃsa, whose mind is sinful.'

9.word_for_word: kim mayā hatayā manda iti-ādi — the words of Devakī's daughter beginning 'What use is there in killing me, fool?'; śrutvā — having heard; devakyā aṣṭamaḥ garbhaḥ na strī bhavitum arhati — continually thinking that Devakī's eighth pregnancy cannot be female; sāmānyena kvacit asti iti jñātvā — knowing only generally that the killer exists somewhere; yuvayoḥ sakhyam sañcintayan — considering the friendship between you two; tvad-gṛhe bhavet iti sambhāvya — supposing that he might be in your house; mat-saṃskāra-liṅgena — from the sign of my performing the rite; āgata-āśaṅkaḥ — one in whom suspicion has arisen; api yadi hantā haniṣyati — if the killer should kill him; tarhi tat tadā naḥ mahān anayaḥ syāt — then that would be a great calamity for us.
9.translation: Having heard the words of Devakī's daughter beginning, 'What use is there in killing me, fool?', Kaṃsa continually thinks that Devakī's eighth pregnancy cannot have been female. Knowing only in general that the one destined to kill him exists somewhere, and considering the friendship between you and Vasudeva, he may suppose that the child is in your house. The sign of my performing the rite would then cause suspicion to arise in him. If he should kill the child, that would be a great calamity for us.

10.word_for_word: dvijāti-saṃskāram — the rite belonging to the twice-born; avaśyaṃ kartavyam — necessarily to be performed; saṃskāra-mātram kevalam — only the essential rite itself; svasti-vācana-pūrvakam — preceded by benedictory recitation; kuru — perform it.
10.translation: Perform only the essential rite that must necessarily be performed for the twice-born, and do it with the recitation of benedictions first.

12.word_for_word: yadūnām apṛthag-bhāvāt — because of bringing the Yadus into non-separation/unity; kutaścit hetoḥ vipratipadyamānānām — of those who for some reason have fallen into disagreement; apṛthag-bhāvaḥ — non-separation; bhāvaḥ bhāvanam — the producing of that condition; anyonya-śikṣayā — through mutual instruction; sarva-aika-mati-karaṇāt — by making all of them of one mind; samyak karṣati ekīkaroti — he draws them together completely, he unifies them; iti saṅkarṣaṇam — therefore he is called Saṅkarṣaṇa; api uśanti — they also call him so; garbha-saṅkarṣaṇam tu — but the drawing of the embryo from the womb; na prakāśayati sma — Garga did not reveal.
12.translation: 'Because of the non-separation of the Yadus' means that, when the Yadus become divided for some reason, he produces their unity, making them all of one mind through mutual counsel. Because he completely draws them together and unifies them, people also call him Saṅkarṣaṇa. Garga, however, did not disclose the other sense of the name—the drawing of the embryo from the womb.

13.word_for_word: asya — of this; tava putrasya — son of yours; ataḥ — therefore; kṛṣṇa iti — 'Kṛṣṇa'; ekam nāma — one name; bhaviṣyati — will be.
13.translation: 'Of this' means 'of this son of yours.' Therefore one of his names will be Kṛṣṇa.

14.word_for_word: prāk ayam — 'formerly this one'; sāmānya-uktyā — by this general statement; ṛṣiḥ ayam janma-antara-gatam nāma kathayati — Nanda thinks that the sage is telling a name belonging to a previous birth; iti nandaḥ manyate sma — thus Nanda understood it; ataḥ — therefore; enam vāsudeva iti sampracakṣate — 'they call him Vāsudeva.'
14.translation: From the general statement 'formerly this one,' Nanda understood that the sage was speaking of a name belonging to one of the child's previous births. Hence Garga says that those who know call him Vāsudeva.

15.word_for_word: guṇa-anurūpāṇi — names corresponding to His qualities; īśvaraḥ sarva-jñaḥ iti-ādīni — such as 'Lord' and 'omniscient'; karma-anurūpāṇi — names corresponding to His deeds; go-patiḥ govardhana-uddharaṇa iti-ādīni — such as 'protector of the cows' and names connected with lifting Govardhana; tāni sarvāṇi — all of them; aham api no veda — even I do not know them all; janāḥ api no viduḥ — nor do ordinary people know them.
15.translation: Names corresponding to His qualities include such designations as 'Lord' and 'omniscient'; names corresponding to His deeds include 'protector of the cows' and names connected with the lifting of Govardhana. I myself do not know all of those names, and ordinary people do not know them either.

16-17.word_for_word: jātaka-phalam āha — he states the result indicated by the nativity; eṣa iti — with the verse beginning 'this one'; ādhāsyat, ādhāsyati — 'will bestow'; anena rakṣyamāṇāḥ — being protected by him; samedhitāḥ ca — and strengthened/prospering; dasyūn vijigyuḥ — the good people conquered the brigands.
16-17.translation: He now states the result indicated by the child's nativity, beginning with 'this one.' 'Ādhāsyat' means 'he will bestow.' The former righteous inhabitants, being protected by him and strengthened under his protection, conquered the brigands.

20.word_for_word: iti ca ātmānam prati samādiśya — having thus given the instruction with reference to ātmānam; ātmānam — the self, or Kṛṣṇa; vā — alternatively; garge gate sati — when Garga had gone; āśiṣām — 'of blessings'; āśīrbhiḥ — by blessings.
20.translation: In the phrase 'having thus instructed with reference to ātmānam,' ātmānam may mean Nanda himself, or it may refer to Kṛṣṇa. When Garga had gone, 'full of blessings' means made full by the blessings he had given.

21.word_for_word: bāla-krīḍā-camatkāraiḥ — by the wonders of childhood play; kṛṣṇaḥ rāmeṇa saṃyutaḥ — Kṛṣṇa together with Rāma; paramānandam ādhatt — bestowed supreme bliss; vraje nanda-yaśodayoḥ — upon Nanda and Yaśodā in Vraja; pūrṇatvam eva darśayan — showing precisely the fullness of that bliss; āha kālena iti — he says, beginning with 'as time passed.'
21.translation: By the wonders of His childhood play, Kṛṣṇa together with Rāma bestowed supreme bliss upon Nanda and Yaśodā in Vraja. Showing precisely the fullness of that bliss, Śuka continues with the words 'as time passed.'

22.word_for_word: anukṛṣya — drawing themselves forward again and again; sarīsṛpantau — moving or crawling very actively; ghoṣāḥ — the jingling sounds; kaṭi-pāda-bhūṣaṇa-kiṅkiṇyaḥ — of the little bells on the waist and foot ornaments; teṣām praghoṣeṇa ninādena — by the resounding sound of those; ruciram — charmingly; teṣām ghoṣāṇām nādena hṛṣṭam manaḥ yayoḥ — whose minds were delighted by the sound of those jingles; lokam itaḥ tataḥ gacchantam anusṛtya — following people moving here and there; tri-caturāṇi padāni anugamya — after following three or four steps; mugdhavat prabhītavat — like innocent, frightened children; mātroḥ anti samīpe upeyatuḥ — they came close to their mothers.
22.translation: 'Anukṛṣya' means drawing themselves forward again and again, and 'sarīsṛpantau' means crawling with great activity. The little bells on their waist and foot ornaments resounded charmingly, and the sound delighted their minds. They would follow people moving here and there for three or four steps and then, like innocent frightened children, come back near their mothers.

23.word_for_word: tadā ca — then; tan-mātarau — their two mothers; nija-sutau — their own sons; upaguhya dorbhyām — embracing them with their arms; pramodam yayatuḥ — experienced delight; ghṛṇayā kṛpayā — through tenderness, compassion; snuvantyau — their breasts flowing; payaḥ-pūrṇa-payodhare satyau — their breasts being full of milk; paṅkena aṅga-rāgeṇa rucirau — the boys beautiful with mud as though it were body-paint; mukham nirīkṣya — seeing the face; mugdham mandam smitam yasmin — on which was a charming gentle smile; alpā daśanāḥ ca yasmin — and in which only a few teeth were visible.
23.translation: Then their two mothers embraced their sons with their arms and experienced delight. Out of tender affection their milk-filled breasts flowed. The boys were lovely, the mud upon them appearing like body-paint. Looking at each child's face, on which there was a charming gentle smile and only a few little teeth, the mothers rejoiced.

24.word_for_word: yarhi — when; aṅganānām darśanīyā kumāra-līlā yayoḥ — when the childhood play of the two had become delightful for the women to behold; tadā — then; antar-vraje — within Vraja; tad-abalāḥ — those women of Vraja; tau prekṣantyaḥ — watching the two boys; vismṛta-gṛha-kṛtyāḥ — forgetting their household duties; hasantyaḥ jahṛṣuḥ — laughing, they rejoiced; tābhyām pragṛhītāni pucchāni yeṣām — whose tails had been seized by the two boys; taiḥ vatsaiḥ itaḥ tataḥ anukṛṣyamāṇau — the boys being dragged here and there by those calves.
24.translation: When the childhood play of the two boys had become a sight delightful for the women, the women of Vraja watched them and, forgetting their household duties, laughed and rejoiced. The boys had grasped the calves by their tails and were being dragged here and there by them.

25.word_for_word: aticcalau — exceedingly restless; aticapalau — exceedingly quick and mischievous; tau — those two; śṛṅgi-ādibhyaḥ niṣeddhum — to restrain them from horned animals and the like; gṛha-ucitāni karmāṇi ca kartum — and to perform the tasks proper to the household; yatra yadā — when; taj-jananyau na śekāte — their mothers were unable; tadā — then; alam manasaḥ anavasthām āpatuḥ — they fell into extreme mental agitation; iti gṛha-saukhyasya parākāṣṭhā darśitā — thus the highest limit of household happiness is shown.
25.translation: The two were extremely restless and mischievous. When their mothers were unable both to keep them away from horned animals and other dangers and to perform their household duties, the mothers fell into intense mental agitation. In this way the very summit of household happiness is shown.

29.word_for_word: kṛṣṇa-cāpala-cauryāṇi — Kṛṣṇa's restlessness and thefts; saha eva akhila-sadmataḥ — from all the houses together; prajalpantyaḥ samāgatya — coming together and chattering about them; gopyaḥ gopyai mudam daduḥ — the gopīs gave delight to the gopī Yaśodā; asamaye — at an improper time, specifically when it was not milking time; krośe sañjāta-hāsaḥ — laughter arose in Him when they shouted at Him; steyam — stolen, acquired by theft; na tu dattam — not something given; tatra api svādu na itarat — even then only what is tasty, not the rest; dadhi ca payaḥ ca atti — He eats curd and milk; bhokṣyan markān prati vibhajya dadāti — when He is going to eat, He divides it and gives portions to the monkeys; teṣām madhye ko'pi na atti cet — if one among them, being full, does not eat; tarhi bhāṇḍam bhinatti — then He breaks the pot; dravyasya alābhe sati — when there is no food to be obtained; sa gṛhāya 'dhakṣyāmi' iti kupitaḥ yāti — He goes away angry, saying to the house, 'I will burn you'; yad vā — alternatively; gṛhāḥ gṛhiṇaḥ — 'houses' means the householders; tebhyaḥ kupitaḥ — angry with them; teṣām tokān bālān — their young children; paryaṅka-ādiṣu suptān — sleeping on beds and the like; upakrośya rodayitvā yāti — He rouses them, makes them cry, and leaves.
29.translation: The gopīs came together from all the houses, chattering about Kṛṣṇa's restlessness and thefts, and thereby gave delight to Yaśodā. 'At an improper time' means when it was not milking time. When they shouted at Him, He began to laugh. 'Stolen' means obtained by theft, not given; and even among stolen things He eats only what is tasty—curd and milk—not the rest. When He wants to eat, He divides the food and gives shares to the monkeys; if one monkey, already satisfied, does not eat, He breaks the pot. Sometimes, when He finds nothing to take, He goes away angry, saying to the house, 'I will burn you.' Alternatively, 'the houses' means the householders: angry with them, He rouses their young children sleeping on beds and the like, makes them cry, and leaves.

30.word_for_word: kalpitaiḥ steya-yogaiḥ — by devised methods of theft; iti uktam tat prapañcayati — he elaborates what was said by that phrase; hastāgrāhye — beyond the reach of the hand; tuṅga-śikya-stha-bhāṇḍeṣu — in vessels kept on high hanging slings; antar-nihite dadhy-ādau — with curd and the like hidden inside; vayunam jñānam yasya — He who has knowledge of it; chidram racayati — makes a hole; tad-vicchidra-racana-ādi-vit — skilled in making such openings; dhvānta-yukte gṛhe — in a dark house; svāṅgam eva artha-pradīpam racayati — He makes His own body a lamp for the object He seeks; viśeṣataḥ dhṛta-maṇi-gaṇam — especially because it bears many jewels; yarhi — when.
30.translation: He now elaborates the phrase 'by devised methods of theft.' When curd and other foods are hidden inside vessels hung high on slings, beyond the reach of His hand, He knows where they are and makes a hole, being skilled in making such openings. In a dark house He makes His own body a lamp for the object He seeks, especially because His body bears many jewels. 'Yarhi' means 'when.'

31.word_for_word: 're re cora' iti ākṣiptaḥ — when accused, 'Hey, thief!'; uśati jalpati — He speaks out; 'tvam eva coraḥ, aham gṛha-svāmī' iti-ādīni — 'You are the thief; I am the master of the house,' and similar words; dhārṣṭyāni prāgalbhyāni — bold, impudent replies; athavā uśati he kamanīye yaśode — alternatively, uśati can be taken as 'O charming Yaśodā'; yad vā uśati vāstau — or as referring to His own shining dwelling; sva-arcite gṛhe mehana-ādīni kurute — He urinates and the like in the house; evaṃ steya-upāyaiḥ viracitā kṛtiḥ yena — though He has carried out acts contrived through methods of theft; tvat-samīpe supratīkaḥ sādhuḥ iva āste — in your presence He sits with an innocent appearance, like a good child; sa-bhaye nayane yasmin — whose eyes show fear; śrī-yuktam mukham — the beautiful face; tad-ālokinībhiḥ — by the women looking at it; vyākhyāta-arthā — the matter having been made known; upalabdhum ākṣeptum na aicchat — she did not wish to rebuke Him.
31.translation: When He is accused, 'Hey, thief!', He boldly replies, 'You are the thief; I am the master of the house,' and says other impudent things. Alternatively, the wording may be taken as an address, 'O charming Yaśodā'; or it may indicate that in His own shining dwelling He urinates and performs similar mischief. Thus, although His deeds have been carried out by contrived methods of theft, when He is in your presence He sits with an innocent appearance, like a perfectly good child. As the women look at His beautiful face and His fearful eyes and make the matter known, Yaśodā, smiling, does not wish to rebuke Him.

32.word_for_word: kadācit apara-aparādha-antare — once, on another occasion involving a different offense; upālabhata — she rebuked Him; tadā tu — but then; mahat āścaryam abhūt — a great wonder occurred; iti kathayan āha — describing this, he says.
32.translation: On another occasion she did rebuke Him for a different offense; but then a great wonder occurred. Describing that event, Śuka now speaks.

33.word_for_word: upālabhya — having rebuked, scolded; nirbhartsya — having reprimanded; bhayena — with fear; sambhrānta-prekṣaṇe — darting or agitated in their glance; akṣiṇī yasya — whose two eyes are such; tam — Him.
33.translation: 'Having rebuked' means having reprimanded Him. His eyes were agitated in their glance because of fear.

34.word_for_word: adānta-ātman — 'O unrestrained one'; capala-gātra — one whose body is restless; rahaḥ — in private; ekānte — in a secluded place.
34.translation: 'Adāntātman' means 'O restless-bodied, unrestrained child.' 'Rahaḥ' means in private, in a secluded place.

35.word_for_word: na aham bhakṣitavān — 'I have not eaten'; na hi bāhyam kiñcit mayā bhakṣyate — indeed, nothing external is eaten by Me; mat-kukṣau ādau eva sarvam asti — because everything already exists within My belly from the beginning; iti bhāvaḥ — this is the implication; samakṣam — directly before the eyes; pratyakṣam — visibly, immediately.
35.translation: In 'I have not eaten,' the implication is: 'Nothing external is really eaten by Me, because everything already exists within My belly from the beginning.' 'Samakṣam' means directly and visibly before the eyes.

36.word_for_word: yadi evam tarhi vyādehi — if that is so, then open [your mouth]; mukham prasāraya — spread open your mouth; vyādatta — He opened it; prasāritavān — He spread it open.
36.translation: 'If that is so, then open it' means 'open your mouth wide.' 'Vyādatta' means that He opened and spread it.

37-38.word_for_word: tatra tasmin mukhe — there, in that mouth; viśvam dadṛśe — she saw the universe; tat prapañcayati — he expands the description; jagat — the moving world; sthāsnu — the stationary world; kham — the atmospheric region; sa-adri-dvīpa-abdhi-bhū-golam — the terrestrial globe together with mountains, islands and oceans; bhū-lokam — the earthly realm; vāyuḥ pravahaḥ — the wind called Pravaha; agniḥ vaidyutaḥ — electrical/fire phenomena; induḥ — the moon; tārakāḥ — the stars; jyotiḥ-cakram — the celestial sphere, Svarga; vaikārikāṇi — the deities; manaḥ — the mind; indriyāṇi taijasāni — the senses, arising from the taijasa aspect; mātrāḥ tāmasāḥ śabda-ādayaḥ — the subtle elements such as sound, arising from the tāmasa aspect.
37-38.translation: There, within that mouth, she saw the universe. Śuka then expands the description: 'jagat' is the moving world, 'sthāsnu' the stationary, and 'kham' the atmospheric region. The terrestrial globe includes its mountains, islands and oceans. The wind is Pravaha; the fire is the electrical fire; together with these are the moon and stars. 'The circle of lights' is the heavenly realm. 'Vaikārika' refers to the deities; although mind is also included in the vaikārika category, it is mentioned separately because it differs from the deities. The senses arise from the taijasa aspect, and the subtle elements such as sound from the tāmasa aspect.

39.word_for_word: evam etat vicitram viśvam saha ekadā eva vīkṣya — thus seeing this entire variegated universe all at once; vicitratām āha — he states its diversity; jīvaḥ ca — the living being; guṇa-kṣobhakaḥ kālaḥ ca — time, which agitates the guṇas; pariṇāma-hetuḥ svabhāvaḥ ca — intrinsic nature, the cause of transformation; janma-hetuḥ karma ca — karma, the cause of birth; tat-saṃskāra-bhūtaḥ āśayaḥ ca — latent disposition, consisting of the impressions of that karma; etaiḥ — by these; liṅgānām carācara-śarīrāṇām bhedaḥ — the differentiation of subtle designations and moving and nonmoving bodies; tatra vrajam ca saha-ātmānam — there she saw Vraja together with herself; sva-sahitam — including herself; sūnoḥ tanau alpe vidārite āsye — within the small body of her son, in His opened mouth; śaṅkām avāpa — she became doubtful/perplexed.
39.translation: Having seen this entire variegated universe all at once, Śuka states the factors of its diversity: the jīva; time, which agitates the guṇas; intrinsic nature, which causes transformation; karma, which causes birth; and the latent dispositions formed by the impressions of karma. Through these arise the distinctions among subtle embodiments and among moving and nonmoving bodies. Then, within the small body of her son—in His opened mouth—Yaśodā saw Vraja together with herself, and she became perplexed.

40.word_for_word: tām eva āha — he states that very doubt; kim svapnaḥ — is this a dream?; paritaḥ vilokya āha na ayam svapnaḥ — looking all around she concludes, this is not a dream; tarhi kim devasya hareḥ māyā — then is it the māyā of the Lord, Hari?; tathā cet anye kim na paśyanti — if so, why do others not see it?; kim vā madīyaḥ eva kaścit buddhi-mohaḥ — or is it some delusion of my own intellect; dhī-viparyāsaḥ — a reversal of cognition; darpaṇe mukhavat — like a face in a mirror; evaṃ tarhi ayam kṛṣṇaḥ api katham antaḥ pratīyate — but then how does this Kṛṣṇa Himself also appear within?; na hi darpaṇe darpaṇa-pratītiḥ — the mirror itself does not appear as its own reflection; antar bahiḥ ca eka-rūpeṇa katham jagat pratīyate — how does the universe appear in the same form both inside and outside?; bimba-pratibimbayoḥ iva parasparam vaiparītyena pratītiḥ syāt — a reflection should appear reversed in relation to its original; athavā — or else; mama eva amuṣya arbhakasya api sataḥ — belonging to this very little child of mine; yaḥ kaścana acintyaḥ ātma-yogaḥ — some inconceivable power of His own; svīyam aiśvaryam — His own majesty; autpattikaḥ — innate; svābhāvikaḥ — natural.
40.translation: Śuka states Yaśodā's very doubt: 'Is this a dream?' Looking all around, she concludes that it is not a dream. 'Then is it the māyā of the Lord, Hari?' But if so, why do others not see it? 'Or is it some delusion of my own intellect, a reversal of cognition like a face in a mirror?' Yet if that were so, how would Kṛṣṇa Himself appear inside the vision? A mirror does not appear as its own reflection. And how could the universe appear in the same form both inside and outside, since an image and its reflection appear mutually reversed? Considering these difficulties, she proposes another possibility: perhaps this little child of mine possesses some inconceivable power of His own—His own innate, natural majesty.

41.word_for_word: caramam pakṣam āśritya — adopting the final alternative; ayam īśvaraḥ iti niścitya — concluding, 'He is the Lord'; āha — she says; cetaḥ — mind; cittam — consciousness; tad-ādibhiḥ na vitarka-gocaram — not within the range of reasoning by mind and the other faculties; jagat yad-āśrayam — that upon which the universe rests; yad-adhiṣṭhānam — its substratum; yena karaṇa-adhiṣṭhātrā — by Him as the ruler of the instruments/senses; yataḥ buddhi-vṛtti-abhivyaktāt — from Him as manifested through the function of intellect; tat-padam — that reality; sudurvibhāvyam — exceedingly difficult to conceive; atyantam acintyam — utterly inconceivable.
41.translation: Adopting the final alternative, Yaśodā concludes, 'He is the Lord,' and speaks accordingly. 'Cetas' means the mind; that reality is not within the reach of reasoning by the mind and the other faculties. The universe rests upon it as its substratum; through it, as the ruler of the instruments of cognition, the universe is apprehended; and from it cognition becomes manifest through the function of intellect. If one asks what that reality is like, the answer is 'exceedingly difficult to conceive'—utterly inconceivable.

42.word_for_word: evaṃ prapañca-pratīti-unnītam tattvam — the reality inferred in this way from the perception of the world; punaḥ jīva-saṃsṛti-hetu-māyā-āśrayatvena unnayanti — she further infers it as the ground of māyā, the cause of the jīva's transmigration; yaśodā-nāmā aham — 'I am the one named Yaśodā'; asau mama patiḥ — 'that man is my husband'; amuṣya vrajeśvarasya akhila-vittapā aham satī jāyā — 'I am the faithful wife of this lord of Vraja and the mistress of all his wealth'; eṣa kṛṣṇaḥ me sutaḥ — 'this Kṛṣṇa is my son'; gopī-ādayaḥ ca madīyāḥ — 'the gopīs and the others are mine'; ittham kumatiḥ — this mistaken conception; yan-māyayā — through whose māyā; sa eṣa me śaraṇam — that very Lord is my refuge.
42.translation: Having thus inferred the supreme reality from the perception of the world, Yaśodā further recognizes it as the ground of māyā, which causes the jīva's transmigration. Through His māyā arises the mistaken conception: 'I am Yaśodā; that man is my husband; I am the faithful wife of the lord of Vraja and mistress of all his wealth; this Kṛṣṇa is my son; the gopīs and the others belong to me.' That very Lord through whose māyā this mistaken understanding arises is my refuge.

43.word_for_word: vaiṣṇavīm — the Vaiṣṇavī māyā; svīyām — His own.
43.translation: 'Vaiṣṇavī' means His own power of māyā.

44.word_for_word: pravṛddhena snehena — by greatly increased affection; kalilam vyāptam hṛdayam yasyāḥ — she whose heart was completely filled; sā purā iva āsīt — she became as she had been before.
44.translation: Her heart became completely filled with greatly increased affection, and she was once again as she had been before.

45.word_for_word: māyā-bala-udrekam āha — he states the overwhelming force of māyā; trayyā — by the threefold Veda; karma-kāṇḍa-rūpayā — in its form as the ritual section; indrādi-rūpeṇa — as Indra and the other deities; upaniṣadbhiḥ — by the Upaniṣads; brahma iti — as Brahman; sāṅkhyaiḥ — by the Sāṅkhya texts; puruṣa iti — as Puruṣa; yogaiḥ — by the Yoga texts; paramātmā iti — as Paramātmā; sātvataiḥ — by the Sātvata scriptures; bhagavān iti — as Bhagavān; upagīyamānam māhātmyam yasya — He whose greatness is sung in these ways.
45.translation: Śuka states the overwhelming force of māyā. In the ritual section of the threefold Veda His greatness is sung through the forms of Indra and the other deities; by the Upaniṣads He is sung as Brahman; by Sāṅkhya as Puruṣa; by Yoga as Paramātmā; and by the Sātvata scriptures as Bhagavān. Such is the Lord whom Yaśodā regarded as her son.

46.word_for_word: ati-vismayena pṛcchati — in extreme wonder the king asks; nanda iti — with the verse beginning 'Nanda'; mahodayam — of great arising or exalted result; mahān udayaḥ udbhavaḥ yasya tat — that whose arising/result is great.
46.translation: In extreme wonder the king asks, beginning with 'Nanda.' 'Mahodayam' means something whose arising or result is exceedingly great.

47.word_for_word: yayoḥ prasannaḥ avatīrṇaḥ — although the Lord graciously descended to those two parents; tau pitarau api yam na anvavindetām — even those parents did not obtain what Nanda and Yaśodā obtained; kṛṣṇasya udāram mahat arbhaka-īhitam — Kṛṣṇa's noble and great deeds as a little child; bāla-līlām — His childhood play; yat ca kavayaḥ gāyanti — which poets still sing; tat yaḥ avindat — the one who obtained that; sa kim śreyaḥ akarot — what extraordinary merit must he have performed?
47.translation: Even the parents to whom the Lord graciously descended did not obtain the experience that Nanda and Yaśodā obtained. The noble, great deeds of Kṛṣṇa as a little child—His childhood play—are still sung by poets. What extraordinary meritorious act, then, must the person who attained such intimacy with Him have performed?

48.word_for_word: brahmaṇaḥ ādeśān — the commands of Brahmā; go-pālana-ādi-lakṣaṇān — consisting of duties such as protecting the cows.
48.translation: The 'commands of Brahmā' were duties characterized by such acts as protecting the cows.

50.word_for_word: sa eva iha droṇaḥ jajñe — that very Droṇa was born here; sa ca nanda iti khyātaḥ — and he became known as Nanda; sā ca dharā — and that Dharā; yaśodā abhavat — became Yaśodā.
50.translation: That very Droṇa was born here and became known as Nanda, while Dharā became Yaśodā.

51.word_for_word: gopa-gopīnām api — even among the cowherd men and women; vastu-svabhāvāt — by the very nature of the reality/situation; asti eva bhaktiḥ — devotion certainly exists; tayoḥ punaḥ — but in those two, Nanda and Yaśodā; nitarām — exceedingly, to a far greater degree.
51.translation: The cowherd men and women also naturally possess devotion to the Lord; but in those two, Nanda and Yaśodā, it existed to an exceedingly greater degree.

52.word_for_word: sva-līlayā — by His own līlā; putra-bhāva-anukāriṇyā — which imitated or conformed to the condition of being their son.
52.translation: He gave them delight through His own līlā, which conformed to and enacted the condition of being their son.
